finding: The cloud bill is not material: about $12.5k/yr, or 1.4% of View 1 cash ($914.5k at $250M CFG-1). The non-labour technology services around it are what is underpriced. Security monitoring has no SIEM or managed detection (MDR) line. FC-010 covers only code and dependency scanning. Yet OA-TEC-003 says triage 'could be outsourced MDR', and SOC 2 CC7 plus sponsor due diligence expect centralised security event monitoring with retained evidence.
evidence: infrastructure-notes s6 lists 'Security tooling, SIEM' as excluded; FC-010 base $3k is described as scanning only; OA-TEC-003 elimination_challenge mentions MDR; no SIEM ingestion is priced (Log Analytics $2.30/GB is priced only as application logs).
proposed_correction: Add FC line 'SIEM / MDR' at low $8k, base $20k, high $50k per year (cloud-native SIEM ingestion plus a small-business MDR service), or show that OA-TEC-003 hours replace it. Keep it separate from FC-010.
estimated_impact: +$8k to $50k/yr View 1 cash (base about +$20k, about +2% of View 1 at $250M)

finding: FC-009 at $6k assumes observability is a paging SaaS bolted onto an existing stack. No stack exists: the owner deferred all monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting on 2026-11-25, Aegis does fault capture only, and Vigila was refuted as an observability system. OA-TEC-001 (19.6 min/day) assumes SLOs, alerts and runbooks that nobody has built or costed.
evidence: echelon-shared notes s1 'Absent' (RP-REG-2026-0001); Aegis 'not responsible for logging, metrics, alerting'; Transitus (listed as covering observability) has no code; FC-009 rationale.
proposed_correction: Raise FC-009 to low $6k, base $12k, high $30k (APM or error tracking, paging for 3-4 people, uptime/synthetics, status page). Add a one-time build of 150-300 h for instrumentation, SLO dashboards, alert routing and runbooks to FC-301, plus about 50 h/yr upkeep to TEC-001.
estimated_impact: +$6k/yr cash plus a one-time $18k to $35k (150-300 h at $118/h)

finding: No cloud support plan is priced, although it is listed as UNKNOWN in the exclusions. A payments-adjacent platform with a 1-hour on-call SLO and a single managed PostgreSQL cluster needs vendor escalation, and sponsor due diligence usually asks about it.
evidence: infrastructure-notes s6: 'Cloud support plans (UNK-001, UNKNOWN; ~$100+/mo)'; ZBI-004 contains no support line.
proposed_correction: Add FC 'cloud support plan' at low $1.2k, base $3.6k, high $12k (Azure Standard about $100/mo; AWS Business max($100, 10% of bill); a higher response tier as the high case).
estimated_impact: +$1k to $12k/yr

finding: The floor uses Azure Front Door Premium ($330/mo) only to get managed WAF rules, and the 35% non-production uplift is applied to it as well. The cheaper options give an equivalent result: Front Door Standard with custom rules ($40), or AWS WAF/CloudFront (about $15). In the other direction, do not add paid DDoS products (Azure DDoS Network Protection about $2,944/mo; AWS Shield Advanced $3,000/mo with a 1-year commitment). Edge-terminated L3/L4 protection plus a WAF is sufficient at this risk and scale.
evidence: infrastructure-notes s1 (AWS floor about 47% lower, mostly Front Door Premium); s3 variants (Standard gives a $642/mo floor); model nonprod = (floor x 12 + 0.1 x variable) x 0.35.
proposed_correction: Set the base platform_fixed_monthly to the Standard/AWS-equivalent (about $120) and keep Premium as the high case. Exclude Front Door from the non-production base. Record explicitly that paid DDoS is out of scope unless a sponsor contract requires it.
estimated_impact: -$3.5k to $4.7k/yr; avoids a possible +$35k/yr error if DDoS were added

target: Analysis.fs mcCost / evaluate (iv = infraVals at Base); ZBP-034 infra_mult
finding: Monte Carlo and the tornado analysis always evaluate infrastructure at its base parameters. Uncertainty enters only through infra_mult (0.7-1.5). The notes, however, show compounded high-case cost per account at 13x base at 1M accounts ($2.27 vs $0.17) and 28x at 100k. The scale-tail risk (identity MAU, SMS, events per account, vCPU per event) therefore never appears in the P90s.
evidence: Analysis.fs: let iv = infraVals inputs (atLevel Base) in mcCost/mcBreakEven/tornado; infrastructure-notes s5 ranges 0.11-2.33 at 100k and 0.02-2.27 at 1M.
proposed_correction: Draw the infrastructure-parameters.csv rows in the Monte Carlo (correlated with activity_mult), or widen infra_mult to 0.5-4 for retail and payroll scale runs.
estimated_impact: Immaterial at 1k-10k accounts; at 1M retail accounts the P90 infrastructure could be about $1-2M/yr rather than about $0.2M

target: OA-TEC-005 backup verification and tenant restore; ZBI-022/023 backups
finding: Tenant-scoped restore in a schema-per-sponsor cluster is not a 1-hour monthly check. Managed point-in-time recovery restores the whole server, so a tenant restore means a new server, then a schema extraction, then reconciliation against the append-only, hash-linked ledger and outbox. That needs purpose-built tooling and a 3-8 h exercise. Ten-year immutable (WORM) backups or archives for ransomware and records requirements are also unpriced, because point-in-time retention ends at 35 days.
evidence: OA-TEC-005 12 x 60 min (12 h/yr); description 'per-tenant restore tested'; CNV-PLT-004 10-year retention; the model prices only backup_multiplier x $0.0475/GB.
proposed_correction: One-time 80-200 h to build restore tooling (FC-301). Set OA-TEC-005 to 12 x 4 h (low 2 h, high 8 h). Add an immutable long-term backup or archive line at $0.5k-3k/yr, scaling with stored GB. Also add 4-8 environment-weeks a year of temporary production-scale environments for the OA-TEC-006/015 load tests and the restore targets (+$0.5k-3k/yr); the 35% non-production share does not cover these.
estimated_impact: +36 to 84 h/yr (about $4k-10k), plus a one-time $10k-24k and $0.5k-3k/yr storage

target: Infrastructure.fs compute scaling; infrastructure-notes s4 thresholds
finding: The architecture's change point is presented as a vCPU threshold (2 vCores to about 730k accounts at base; about 23k in the high case). Compute will not be the first limit to bind. More likely triggers, in order: (1) the first institutional sponsor contractually demanding a dedicated database, customer-managed key or region (C3), which can happen at sponsor 1; (2) December and year-end batch work (statements, tax receipts, unit/NAV allocations, reconciliation queries) on the same primary as the database-backed queues, since the event model counts only durable events and no read or reporting load; (3) one region, one primary and a deferred observability stack giving an RTO that sponsors will not accept; (4) schema count and migration fan-out above roughly 50-100 sponsors.
evidence: events_per_vcpu_hour counts durable events only (INF-DB-010..012); OA-TEC-006/015 December load tests exist but no reporting-load driver does; CNV-ARC-001 'broker or workflow engine only on measured evidence'; sponsorsFor caps sponsors at 20 in Outputs.fs, hiding many-sponsor configurations (PG-CF).
proposed_correction: Replace the single vCPU threshold with explicit trigger metrics: queue lag p99 in December, primary CPU above 60% during the statement run, a sponsor isolation clause, and sponsor count above 50. Price a read replica for reporting ($130-250/mo) from about 50k accounts or the first year-end. Run the RM-05 benchmark before acceptance.
estimated_impact: Cost small (+$1.6k-3k/yr per replica), but the architecture review should be planned at about 50k accounts or the first isolation request, not 730k

finding: C3 prices each isolated sponsor database at cloud list price only ($5.5k/yr). Each isolated database is in practice another production system. It needs its own migrations, major-version upgrades, restore tests, DR drills, monitoring and key rotation, yet the TECHOPS rows driven per_platform (TEC-005/006/011/015) do not scale with the number of isolated databases.
evidence: Infrastructure.fs: isolation = isolatedSponsors x isolated_db_monthly; OA-TEC-005/006/011/015 driver = per_platform.
proposed_correction: Add per-isolated-database engineering of 40-80 h/yr (TEC-005/006/011 share), and note that isolation can be triggered by contract below 50k accounts.
estimated_impact: +$5k-9k/yr labour per isolated sponsor (about doubling the C3 increment)

target: ZBI-020 retention_years; Infrastructure.fs storage; ZBI-041 egress
finding: Several storage and egress details are mis-scaled but small. (a) Retention: 7 years are kept online, but records must be retained 10 years after the transaction, and an append-only, hash-chained ledger is in practice never pruned, so online data grows without limit. (b) Storage is priced at steady state (7 x annual volume) even in year 1, which overstates it early. (c) Stepped SKUs (2 to 4 vCores, 128 GB to 512 GB to 4 TB) are priced continuously, e.g. 0.74 extra vCPU at 1M accounts. (d) Egress of 15 MB per account-year may be low for a .NET WebAssembly bundle (several MB compressed, re-downloaded after each of about 50 releases a year).
evidence: infrastructure.csv peak_vcpu 2.74 at 1M accounts priced as fractional; infrastructure-notes s4 (4 TB provisioning, 4 vCores at 1M); CNV-PLT-004.
proposed_correction: Model storage as a cumulative year-by-year schedule with retention of at least 10 years and archive tiering. Use stepped SKUs. Raise egress_gb_per_acct high to 0.15.
estimated_impact: Below $10k/yr at 1M accounts; under $1k at 10k

finding: Base log volume of 15 GB/mo excludes the audit logs that SOC 2 and sponsors will ask for: pgaudit on regulated tables, WAF/Front Door access logs, and identity sign-in logs. Each can exceed application logs. At $2.30/GB in the Log Analytics analytics tier, 50-100 GB/mo costs about $100-220/mo more.
evidence: infrastructure-notes C1 Log Analytics 15 GB/mo; prices s2 Basic $0.50 and Auxiliary $0.05 tiers available.
proposed_correction: Raise base logs to 40-60 GB/mo, with a design rule to send audit/WAF logs to Basic/Auxiliary tiers.

target: Database architecture: role per sponsor, database-backed queues
finding: Two operational costs of the chosen PostgreSQL pattern are missing. (1) A role per sponsor fragments connection pools: a pool per role means connections grow with sponsors x pool size, so a pooler is needed (PgBouncer built-in on Azure; RDS Proxy about $22/mo on AWS). (2) Queue, outbox and timer tables churn (insert, update, delete), unlike the append-only ledger. They need autovacuum tuning and bloat monitoring, and the 1.25 overhead factor assumes append-only rows.
evidence: CNV-ARC-001 (schema and role per sponsor, RLS, outbox, timer table); ZBI-019 index_overhead rationale 'append-only rows never update'; Echelon.Execution not benchmarked.
proposed_correction: Add a pooler line (AWS) and 20-40 h/yr of queue and database hygiene to OA-TEC-011. Include connection count and bloat in the RM-05 benchmark.
estimated_impact: +$0.3k/yr cash and +20-40 h/yr; prevents a sponsor-count ceiling

target: OA-TEC-010 two-approver review; Workload.fs authMinutes; Simulation arrivals
finding: The two-approver review is costed wrongly in two ways. (1) The second approval goes to the 'authorizer' role, which is the AUTH pool at controller rates, so 0.3 x 40 min = 12 min of one reviewer, instead of to engineers. CNV-PLT-010 requires two non-author engineering approvers per control-relevant change. (2) A volume of 300 changes a year is low for an AI-assisted codebase that inserted about 288k lines in 6 days, with 376 Unbound commits over the same period. AI-generated pull requests are larger and need deeper review.
evidence: Workload.fs: authMinutes = authorized x minutes x independent_review_share, assigned to 'authorizer'; arrivals route auth to poolOf 'authorizer' = AUTH; OA-TEC-010 freq 100/300/800, 40 min; FC-302 rationale (288k lines in 6 days).
proposed_correction: Model OA-TEC-010 as ENG minutes = changes x 2 approvers x 45 min, plus author rework at 20%. Use base 500 changes (high 1,500). Route nothing from TEC-010 to AUTH.
estimated_impact: ENG +550 h/yr base (200 h becomes about 750 h), +$65k; high case +2,000 h

finding: The rule of author plus two non-author approvers is met only by counting the founder as the third engineer. Every control-relevant change then needs all three people. Each person is absent 25 business days a year, and the founder has 400 h for Unbound across 30 initiatives, so releases and emergency fixes will regularly be blocked. Alternatively the founder becomes the routine reviewer, which consumes founder hours the model does not count. A security fix on a control-relevant module cannot wait for the founder.
evidence: headline-staffing ENG: dedicated 2, named 3, founder 314 h; ZBP-013 absence 20-30 days; echelon-shared s6 'Approver capacity ... cannot be met' with one human; DF-ASR-2026-7B20 conflict.
proposed_correction: Require 4 named engineering approvers (3 dedicated + founder), or 3 dedicated plus a contracted, access-provisioned reviewer retainer of 100-200 h/yr. Add an emergency-change procedure with retrospective second approval.
estimated_impact: +$106k-212k/yr (a third engineer) or +$17k-34k/yr (reviewer retainer at $150-170/h)

finding: On-call is effectively unmodelled. The simulation gives every pool zero capacity at weekends and converts the 1-hour SLA into one business day. Weekend and night incidents (including around 31 December and the ACH cut-offs) therefore wait for Monday, and no standby cost appears. With 2 engineers plus a founder, 24/7 cover is a 1-in-3 rota, which tends to burn people out and drive turnover, and no pager stipend or time off in lieu is included.
evidence: Simulation.fs capacity: if isWeekend d then 0.0; arrivals: sla = max 1.0 (SlaHours/24); OA-TEC-001 365 x 19.6 min.
proposed_correction: Add an on-call cost: stipend $300-600 per person-week of cover (52 weeks), plus out-of-hours incident time at 1.5x. Reduce productive hours by 3-5% for time off in lieu. Model a 4-person rota as the sustainable minimum.
estimated_impact: +$16k-31k/yr stipend, +60-150 h/yr out-of-hours; strengthens the case for a 3rd/4th engineer

finding: Integration maintenance is scaled per sponsor (20 x 2 h = 40 h per sponsor-year). The cited evidence prices it per integration ($9.4k, about 63-80 h, per custom integration per year), and most integrations are platform-level and shared. These include: the ODFI/Nacha file origination; the payment partners Chariot, then PayPal; the external investment manager or custodian; identity and bank verification (Stripe, Persona, Plaid/Financial Connections); email and SMS; and the accounting export. Each has API deprecations, certificate and SFTP key rotation, recertification and rule changes. With one sponsor, the model carries about 45 h/yr for all of them.
evidence: OA-TEC-012 evidence 'charity-network 20 ($9.4k per custom integration per year)'; driver per_sponsor; OD-P-PAY, OD-M-07; ZBP-027/028 integration failures 6 x 8 h; IRS/OFAC connectors are covered separately by Beneficium upkeep (25 h/connector).
proposed_correction: Add a platform-level row: about 8-12 integrations x 40-80 h/yr (base 10 x 60 = 600 h). Keep per-sponsor work for sponsor-specific mappings only (20 h).
estimated_impact: +450-900 h/yr at 1-2 sponsors (+$53k-106k; about +0.3-0.6 FTE)

target: TECHOPS inventory: absence of defect remediation and enhancement
finding: No activity covers fixing production defects or the sponsor-driven change backlog. OA-TEC-019 (40 h/sponsor) covers diagnosis only. OA-TEC-011 (246 h) covers migrations, upgrades and flag hygiene. A new, AI-generated financial system of about 27k F# lines will have escaped defects in its first 2-3 years. Each fix passes through test, the two-approver review and the release rings, and ledger defects also need correction postings. Industry norms put sustaining engineering at 15-20% of build effort per year.
evidence: OA-TEC-011 description; OA-TEC-019 'cases that need engineering diagnosis'; FC-302 $1.5M (baseline $1.94M); Unbound has no production history and no CI.
proposed_correction: Add OA-TEC-022 'Defect remediation and sustaining change' at low 400 h, base 900 h, high 1,800 h per year, per platform (equivalent to 7-14% of a $1.5-1.94M build at $118/h). Scale +10% per additional sponsor for configuration requests.
estimated_impact: +$47k-212k/yr; base about +$106k (+0.6 FTE)

finding: No engineering line implements regulatory change. Known changes already in flight include: the 2025 federal tax law's charitable changes from 2026 (0.5%-of-AGI floor for itemizers, a cap on the deduction benefit, and a non-itemizer deduction that excludes DAF gifts), which affect donor statements and receipts; the Nacha 2026 fraud-monitoring rule phases; and the still-pending Treasury DAF regulations. Recurring changes include IRS form and schema years, OFAC list formats and state unclaimed-property rules.
evidence: operational-activities: no TECHOPS row for regulatory change; compliance activities cover policy, not code; FC-007 Nacha audit fee only.
proposed_correction: Add OA-TEC-023 'Regulatory change implementation' at low 80 h, base 200 h, high 500 h per year, per platform, including a two-approver review.
estimated_impact: +$9k-59k/yr (base about +$24k)

target: OA-TEC-007 vulnerability management and dependency updates
finding: OA-TEC-007 comes to about 82 h/yr after the AI factor (12 x 480 min x 0.85). Patching spans several stacks: the .NET LTS cadence (.NET 8 support ends November 2026, so a .NET 10 migration falls in year 1); the F# compiler and WebAssembly toolchain; the Limen TypeScript kernel and its npm tree; container base images; PostgreSQL major-version upgrades through a pilot tool (Strata 0.1.1); and the release churn of Echelon components (Praxis had 40 tags in 4 months). Critical CVEs arrive in bursts with a 168 h SLA, not evenly through the year.
evidence: OA-TEC-007 minutes 240/480/960 monthly, AI-ASSISTED; echelon-shared s6 'Release churn'; no repository runs SAST or dependency scanning; Unbound has no CI.
proposed_correction: Raise TEC-007 to a base of 16 h/month (high 30), and add 80-160 h one-time for each LTS or PostgreSQL major upgrade every 2 years. Model critical CVEs as incidents.

target: FC-101 shared component maintenance; ZBP-016 founder_hours; Echelon reliance
finding: Unbound's dependency on immature Echelon components is costed as founder time that is not cash and capacity that does not exist. Transitus (job queue, schema governance, observability) has no code. Echelon.Execution (2,558 lines) is incubated in Unbound and has not been benchmarked. Strata is a v0.1.1 pilot. Monitoring is absent. Fides supports GitHub sign-in only, and Folio has no PDF engine. Each of these has Unbound as its only consumer, so it is in effect Unbound code. Yet FC-101 ($52.5k share) is founder-performed and excluded from View 1. The founder is also allocated 400 h in staffing, about 450 h of assurance work and roughly 260 h for FC-101, competing for 1,800 h across 30 initiatives.
evidence: echelon-shared notes s1, s6, s7 (incubated libraries 100% Unbound; founder about 1,800 h; 57+26 repos); FC-101 'founder-performed so non-cash'; ZBP-016 base 400.
proposed_correction: Treat Execution, Transitus (or its replacement) and Strata as Unbound engineering: add 300-600 h/yr to ENG, in cash, in View 1. Add a founder-capacity constraint check: Unbound founder hours across staffing, FC-101 and assurance must not exceed the owner's allocation. Make replacing Transitus with mature open-source or managed services an explicit decision.
estimated_impact: +$35k-71k/yr cash in View 1; removes a hidden key-person dependency

target: Unbound CI/CD, infrastructure as code, signed builds (FC-301; OA-TEC-009)
finding: OA-TEC-009 (signed builds; synthetic, canary and production rings) and OA-TEC-010 (approval enforcement) assume a CI/CD pipeline. Unbound has no CI and no Praxis installation, and no repository runs SAST, dependency or secret scanning. The availability brief also rules out Terraform. Without infrastructure as code, DR rebuilds and SOC 2 change-management evidence depend on manual console changes.
evidence: echelon-shared s1 (no CI workflows); s3 (no SAST in 11 CI setups); infrastructure-notes s1 'No Kubernetes, Terraform'; ZBI-004 includes $18/mo CI.
proposed_correction: One-time 300-700 h in FC-301 for the pipeline, signing, SBOM, environment promotion and IaC (Bicep/CloudFormation/OpenTofu). Add 60-120 h/yr upkeep. Budget CI minutes beyond the Team allowance ($20-100/mo).
estimated_impact: One-time $35k-83k; +$7k-15k/yr

target: Simulation incident handling; TEC-002/TEC-019 per_sponsor drivers; staffing-thresholds.csv ENG
finding: Incident load is mis-shaped in both directions. (a) OA-TEC-002 (50 h) and TEC-019 (40 h) scale linearly per sponsor. In a shared monolith most incidents are platform-wide and are triaged once; only communication scales with sponsors. This drives the steep ENG thresholds (PG-INST 6 FTE at 7,500 accounts; PG-HNW 7 at 40k, i.e. 20 sponsors). (b) Seeded incidents must be completed within one business day, and adding people is assumed to shorten the fix linearly, which inflates simulated headcount. (c) The other way: the 50 h of TEC-002 is spread across every day of the year, so incident lumpiness at 1-2 sponsors disappears.
evidence: Simulation.fs arrivals spread h x weight per day; runPool places incidents with SlaDays 1 at the head; Outputs.fs sponsorsFor = assets/500M capped at 20; staffing-thresholds.csv.
proposed_correction: Split TEC-002 into a platform part (base 40 h + 3 incidents x 16 h) and a per-sponsor communication part (8 h). Model incidents as lumps with a 3-5 business-day completion target and a cap on concurrent engineers. Re-derive the ENG thresholds.
estimated_impact: At 10-20 sponsors ENG is probably overstated by 2-3 FTE (-$0.4M to $0.6M/yr); at 1-2 sponsors roughly neutral

finding: The engineering cost of $212.4k loaded ($118/h x 1,800 h) is a generic software engineer rate. The roles need F#/.NET, PostgreSQL internals, payments and SOC 2 security, and a 1-in-3 on-call rota. The F# talent pool is small, so expect recruiter fees (20-25% of first-year salary), longer vacancies and a retention premium. The model has no recruiting, onboarding or turnover cost for engineers.
evidence: roles.csv engineering 176.4k/212.4k/248.4k (PAR-006 x 1800 h); FC-206 G&A recruiting only in the standalone view.
proposed_correction: Raise the base to about $235k (high $280k). Add engineering recruiting and turnover of $15k-30k per engineer-year (one replacement every 3-4 years plus a fee) in View 1.
estimated_impact: +$46k-80k/yr at 2 engineers

target: FC-301 / FC-302 development cost vs $1.94M baseline
finding: FC-302's base ($1.5M) is set below the competitive-displacement build baseline ($1.94M) even though no effort records exist. Its rationale says the line counts are output, not effort. FC-301 cash ($0.5M, agent usage plus contract review) omits items still to be built: CI/IaC, observability, donor identity (no Echelon provider), a PDF engine (Folio has none), payment-partner adapters, Transitus's scope, restore tooling, an independent secure-code review of AI-generated control modules, and engineers hired before revenue (months_to_first_revenue 12) if these are not counted as working capital.
evidence: fixed-costs FC-301/FC-302 rationale; competitive-displacement 10-zero-touch-administration-economics.md ($1.94M for MD-3/4/5); echelon-shared s7 'Shared but absent'.
proposed_correction: Set the FC-302 base to $1.94M until effort is measured. Itemise FC-301 with the missing build lines (about 1,200-2,500 h, or $140k-300k) plus a secure-code review ($30k-60k). State whether pre-revenue engineer salaries sit in FC-301 or in working capital, and do not count them twice.
estimated_impact: View 2 amortisation +$88k/yr (0.44M/5); View 1 one-time cash +$170k-360k

finding: Validating AI-generated code costs more than review time. It needs a maintained test oracle (ledger property tests, reconciliation invariants, mutation testing on control modules) and evaluation runs whenever models or prompts change. Two things are unpriced: OA-TEC-021's external cost (UNKNOWN), and the Unbound share of FC-104 agent usage ($8.4k base), which looks low if agents do most of the maintenance coding.
evidence: OA-TEC-021 external_cost_per_event UNKNOWN; FC-104 24k x 0.35; 'agent usage cost unmeasured'; no Praxis telemetry in Unbound.
proposed_correction: Add 100-200 h/yr of test-oracle upkeep to TEC-011 or the new TEC-022. Price evaluation and agent tokens at $5k-25k/yr for Unbound until telemetry measures them.

finding: The modelled 1,714 h/yr for ENG (2 dedicated plus 314 founder hours, 58.8% utilisation at $250M) is credible only as keep-the-lights-on operations with feature work frozen. Adding the omissions at base gives about 4,700 h, or about 3.6 FTE at 1,534 productive hours and 85% utilisation: review fix +550, platform integrations +600, defects/sustaining +900, regulatory +200, patching +150, Echelon components +400, on-call/out-of-hours +100, restore +60, CI/observability upkeep +100. 2 engineers plus the founder cannot sustain this. 3 engineers plus the founder is the floor, and 4 engineers is needed for the approval rule, continuity and on-call.
evidence: headline-staffing.csv ENG 1,714 h/2.0/named 3; results.md s4; productive hours 6.5 x (261-25) = 1,534; sum of the maintenance findings in this file.
proposed_correction: Rebase ENG to 3.5-4 FTE at 1-2 sponsors (low 3, high 5). Then re-run break-even, since View 1 at $250M rises by about 25-46%.
estimated_impact: +$212k-425k/yr View 1 cash; break-even at 20 bps rises from about $0.5B to about $0.6-0.7B (re-run needed)
